notes:
Three connected fixes in the agent review loop, all of them about the platform telling the truth to the person who approves a change.

(1) Audit row completeness (the v0.2.26 gap). When a generation was allowed through because the operator had declared an upstream echo name, the persisted agent_request.generate audit row recorded requested and served model but not the declaration — so the stored record showed 'served differs from requested yet a candidate was produced' with no visible basis, indistinguishable from the guard being bypassed. The declaration is now written into that audit row (absent when there is no declaration, exactly as before).

(2) Candidates are now checked against the finding's own rule, and the platform shows its own result. In the P4 production acceptance run (desc5 r4) the generation prose told the reviewer the description satisfied the 120-160 character rule while the candidate was 162 characters, and nothing in the platform had ever checked that claim. Candidates from a finding that has a machine-checkable acceptance criterion (page:title 30-60, page:description 120-160) now carry a deterministic check performed by the platform, displayed ABOVE the model's prose: measured length, the interval, and — when out of range — a plain statement that the item can still be submitted for human judgement. This marks and displays; it never rejects the batch, never rewrites a candidate, and never touches stores or execution paths (the underlying finding is a warn-level suggestion). Rules whose acceptance is not machine-checkable (contains-keyword, no-stuffing) are stated as unchecked rather than implied. The length thresholds now live in one shared table used by both the deep-audit finding and the action catalogue, so the prose shown to the model and the platform's own criterion cannot drift apart. Deliberately narrow: a finding whose acceptance is not a length interval gets no check at all rather than a mislabelled one.

(3) The review UI now shows which model produced the candidate. requested/served/declared were already returned once by the generate response, but later reads had nothing, so the reviewer approving a batch could not see which model produced it or whether a declared rename was used. The candidate message itself now records the generation (migration 051), and the review surfaces render it: 'this batch was generated by X', plus, when a declared rename was in force, 'upstream reported Y, admitted under the operator's declaration; the platform records this faithfully and does not claim the two are equivalent'. A candidate that a human edited in place records no model — the edited values are not the model's work, and the UI says nothing rather than attributing them.

Also fixed: the thin web schema silently dropped originRef.findingId (zod strips undeclared keys), so the front end could never see which finding a request came from. Both this field and the new generation field are now declared, and a browser check fails if either is stripped again.

Database: additive migration 051 (agent_request_messages.generation jsonb, nullable, no backfill, CHECK jsonb_typeof). Historical messages simply have no generation recorded — displayed as nothing, never inferred from current settings. Because this release carries a migration, an upgrade stops the worker and dispatcher first, as with v0.2.24 and v0.2.12.

Rollback target: v0.2.26 application images only. Migration 051 is additive and nullable, so v0.2.26 code runs unchanged on the new schema (it ignores the column); the acceptance-check display and the model line simply disappear. No persisted record shape outside that new column changes.

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.26.

Validation before tagging, on a clean worktree of commit 134d457 (this release commit adds only this manifest file): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm --filter api test; pnpm typecheck; pnpm build; the BFF routing verification across the ip/domain/tunnel Caddy templates; the CI static entry-point and bootstrap-contract checks including the 23 Python retention cases; disposable PostgreSQL 16 with both migration passes and the five agent suites (125/125); browser verification of the acceptance-check and generation display with real components and real Chrome (18 checks), and of the AI settings declaration fields. Exact counts are recorded in docs/286.

One timing-sensitive test in the API suite (crawlConcurrency, a wall-clock assertion with a 400 ms bound) failed once on this machine under load and passed on the immediate re-run; it exercises the crawler, which this release does not touch.

Not asserted here: a re-run of the P4 production acceptance. Item 1032 remains at 162 characters until its observation window closes on 2026-11-04, and the 0.9.1 readback-channel verification (a real content_edit or internal_link_add production action) is scheduled separately.
